construct_or_mutation: human FGF8b Q23-E186 with N-terminal GAMG (residues 19-22) left after TEV cleavage, uniformly 15N or 13C/15N labeled
other_conditions: 5% D2O, 0.5 mM TSP; 350 µL sample; sample concentration listed as 285-600 µM per spectrum in Table 1; related structures: 2FDB (FGF8b in complex with FGFR2c, X-ray, gN helix formed); per-residue T1, T2, NOE, S2, Te and model are in the supplement spreadsheet only (FGF8b-dynamics sheet); first 13 N-terminal residues absent from 2FDB were modelled; the supplement sheet labels residues with construct numbering offset by 18 from the paper numbering (for example label D73 = D91)
caveat_note: The card lists 298.5 K and 700 MHz while this paper records relaxation at 298 K and 600 MHz (700 MHz was used only for the 15N-NOESY), and no BMRB id for the relaxation data is given; the paper deposits assignments as BMRB 51832. The text describes N-terminal motions as picosecond, whereas the supplement lists Te of about 1 ns for residues 33-45; this disagreement is unresolved. The error of Te for D91 (2.784 ns) exceeds its value, so the Te of the D91-S95 loop is weakly determined for D91 and S95. The assignment of sheet labels to paper numbering rests on matching residue letters (D, T, F, G, S).
experiment: 15N T1, T2 and {1H}-15N NOE at 600 MHz (HSQC-based pseudo-3D, interleaved), model-free analysis with TENSOR2
author_claim: The protein is dynamically stable for residues 50-178; the N-terminus is highly flexible with picosecond motions; residues 33-45 show a plateau of partly restricted S2 where the gN helix sits in 2FDB; the D91-S95 loop shows low-amplitude nanosecond motions (Te) with little change in S2.
anchor: the nanosecond mobility is also observed in the D91-S95 loop (decreased T1 and the presence of nanosecond motions (T e ) in the results of model-free analysis)

construct_or_mutation: human FGF8b Q23-E186 with N-terminal GAMG (residues 19-22) left after TEV cleavage, uniformly 15N or 13C/15N labeled
other_conditions: 5% D2O, 0.5 mM TSP; 350 µL sample; sample concentration listed as 285-600 µM per spectrum in Table 1; related structures: 2FDB (FGF8b in complex with FGFR2c, X-ray, gN helix formed); chemical shifts from 3D triple-resonance spectra; gN helix is residues 33-40; helical propensity at N-terminus residues 35-50; SSP gives up to 0.1 helix probability; N-terminus disordered up to residue 50
alt_state_structure: 2FDB: FGF8b in complex with FGFR2c, gN helix formed and packed in the hydrophobic groove of the FGFR2c D3 domain (Analysis of chemical shifts; Figure 2)
caveat_note: The card lists 298.5 K and 700 MHz while this paper records relaxation at 298 K and 600 MHz (700 MHz was used only for the 15N-NOESY), and no BMRB id for the relaxation data is given; the paper deposits assignments as BMRB 51832. This is a chemical-shift inference about conformational state, not a measured exchange process; the receptor-bound state is assigned from the crystal structure of the complex, and no exchange between free and helical states is measured. 'Formed only on binding' is the authors' hypothesis.
experiment: TALOS-N, SSP and random-coil-index (RCI-S2) analysis of backbone chemical shifts at 298 K (900 MHz spectra)
author_claim: The gN helix (33-40) seen in the FGFR2c complex crystal structure is not formed in free FGF8b; the N-terminus is disordered up to residue 50 and probably becomes structured only on binding the FGFR2 D3 domain.
anchor: it is clear that the gN helix (residues 33–40) is not formed.
